request.spec:
A user can set a preview date on their screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show
it, or nothing). While it is set, every figure on the screen for that user is shown as if the
sheet's today were that date (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and
rate in force), over the sheet's current records; every change still uses the sheet's real today,
and nothing that a change of today does (snapshots, scores, auto-closing) happens. The preview
belongs to the signed-in user's screen.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A user can set a preview date on their screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show
it, or nothing). While it is set, every figure on the screen for that user is shown as if the
sheet's today were that date (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and
rate in force), over the sheet's current records; every change still uses the sheet's real today,
and nothing that a change of today does (snapshots, scores, auto-closing) happens. The preview
belongs to the signed-in user's screen.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
You can now set a preview date on your screen, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**How it works**
- **Panel** (`features/preview/preview.slot.tsx`): a date entry, a set button and a clear button, with the preview date shown in `sheet-preview` (empty when none is set). The date is kept in the browser address (the `preview` search parameter). So it belongs to that one screen: another signed-in user doesn't see it, and it survives reloading the sheet. Setting or clearing it re-reads everything on the screen.
- **Reads** (`api/http.ts`): while a preview is set, every read sends the date along. Saves and other changes never send it.
- **Server** (`preview/PreviewView.java`): when a read carries a preview date, it runs inside a database transaction that first sets the sheet's today to that date and is always rolled back. It works the same way as the existing "as of" view, but over the sheet's current records rather than a snapshot. Only the stored today is replaced, so nothing else a change of today does (snapshots, scores, auto-closing) runs. Nothing is written and nothing goes to the audit file.
- **Real today kept for changes:** the sheet itself still reports its real today. So `sheet-today`, default dates and every change keep using it. Most figures (late charges, overdue, aged amounts, the rate in force) are worked out in the browser from the sheet's today. For those, `useSheetToday` now returns the preview date while one is set. I also pointed the sheet-compare figures at it, since they read the sheet's today directly.
- **With "as of" also set:** the as-of date wins and the preview is ignored.

**A change outside the request.** "Preview date scenario 1" doesn't use the preview at all. It failed because when a statement is taken, its due-total left out the person's parts of claims shared with them. The rollup and the screen count those parts. I changed `statement/TakeStatement.java` to count them the same way: it adds the parts of claims shared with the person, takes out the parts of their own claims shared with others, and doesn't show "n/a" for someone holding a part. The test expected this, but it changes what statements record, so you may want to review it separately.
